findings.issue_text: request.referer is attacker-controlled and only checked at initial page load, so X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is set unconditionally for any request with a spoofed Referer matching embeddable_host, allowing clickjacking/framing from arbitrary origins
import_remote/open(url) via open-uri fetches user/feed-supplied URLs without restricting scheme or host, enabling SSRF through feed_polling_url or the embed retrieval flow

absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src starting with '/' and doesn't sanitize javascript: or other unsafe schemes; combined with raw_html cook_method rendered unsanitized via raw post.cooked, this allows stored XSS from RSS feeds or embedded remote content

poll_feed.rb can set url to a non-URL feed GUID when blank or not matching http(s) pattern, which later causes URI(url) to raise an uncaught URI::InvalidURIError in absolutize_urls, breaking the whole feed poll for one bad item

race condition between the embed_url existence check and TopicEmbed.create! inside the transaction allows concurrent PollFeed/TopicRetriever jobs to create duplicate topics, risking an unrescued RecordNotUnique error
$redis.setnx lock in topic_retriever.rb is not released or handled if perform_retrieve raises, causing legitimate retries within 60s to be silently dropped after a failed fetch
removal of the --category option from the disqus.thor CLI task changes existing import behavior with no migration path for existing scripts
no test coverage exists for import_remote, SSRF-relevant URL handling, or XSS/sanitization of imported raw HTML content

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src starting with '/' and doesn't sanitize javascript: or other unsafe schemes; combined with raw_html cook_method rendered unsanitized via raw post.cooked, this allows stored XSS from RSS feeds or embedded remote content

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html`, and `Post#cook` now returns `raw` directly when `cook_method == :raw_html`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`. `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href`/`src` values starting with `/` and does not sanitize or filter unsafe schemes/HTML (e.g., `<script>`, `onerror=`, `href="javascript:..."`). The embed view then renders this content with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so imported feed/remote content can be stored and rendered as-is, enabling stored XSS if the feed/page content contains malicious HTML/attributes/schemes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb can set url to a non-URL feed GUID when blank or not matching http(s) pattern, which later causes URI(url) to raise an uncaught URI::InvalidURIError in absolutize_urls, breaking the whole feed poll for one bad item

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, when `i.link` is blank or not `http(s)`, it assigns `url = i.id`. However, `TopicEmbed.import` immediately returns unless `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, so a non-URL GUID (e.g., `tag:...`, `urn:...`) will be ignored and will not reach `absolutize_urls` (and thus cannot trigger `URI(url)` there). The proposed failure chain (“non-URL feed GUID → URI(url) raises in absolutize_urls → breaks poll”) is therefore not verifiable from the diff as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: race condition between the embed_url existence check and TopicEmbed.create! inside the transaction allows concurrent PollFeed/TopicRetriever jobs to create duplicate topics, risking an unrescued RecordNotUnique error

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank, enters a `Topic.transaction` and later calls `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. There is a unique DB index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). With concurrent jobs (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` iterating items and `TopicRetriever` fetching the same URL), two workers can both see no existing row and both create a topic/post, then the second `create!` will hit the unique index and raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or adapter equivalent). The code does not rescue this, so the job/request can error. This is a classic check-then-insert race present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: $redis.setnx lock in topic_retriever.rb is not released or handled if perform_retrieve raises, causing legitimate retries within 60s to be silently dropped after a failed fetch

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, the Redis key is used as a 60-second throttle, not a lock that must be explicitly released. When `setnx` succeeds, the code immediately sets `expire(retrieved_key, 60)` before returning `false` (allowing `perform_retrieve` to run). If `perform_retrieve` later raises, the key will still expire after 60 seconds, so it is neither “not released” nor “silently dropped” beyond the intended throttle window. The inability to retry within 60 seconds after a failed fetch is consistent with the comment “Throttle other users to once every 60 seconds,” not a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: removal of the --category option from the disqus.thor CLI task changes existing import behavior with no migration path for existing scripts

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the CLI option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` is removed and the associated logic that looked up `category_id` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator.new(...)` is also deleted. The import path now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` without any category parameter. This is a verifiable behavioral change that will break existing scripts/automation that call `disqus:import` with `--category` (option no longer recognized) and removes the ability to import into a chosen category via this task.

adjudication_records.issue_text: no test coverage exists for import_remote, SSRF-relevant URL handling, or XSS/sanitization of imported raw HTML content

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` (open-uri) and then imports `doc.content` as a post with `cook_method: :raw_html`, causing `Post#cook` to return `raw` directly and the embed view to render it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. There is no sanitization applied to RSS content in `Jobs::PollFeed` (it uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` only) and `TopicEmbed.import` appends an `<a href='#{url}'>` without escaping beyond a loose `^https?://` regex, so XSS/injection risk is plausible and grounded in the code. Additionally, the added specs cover `.import` but do not cover `.import_remote` at all, nor do they test URL safety/SSRF constraints or HTML sanitization behavior for raw imported content.
